title: US–China truce extension expires — Busan/Kuala Lumpur suspensions (MOFCOM export controls, USTR Sec. 301 maritime action, BIS Affiliates Rule) run to 2027-01-10
source: NEWS: the 2026-11-09 two-month extension, read from three sides. US, primary and read direct 2026-11-12: USTR Notice of Modification of Section 301 Action, FR doc 2026-22867 (federalregister.gov, publication date 2026-11-10; the action 'further suspended through 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on January 9, 2027'), and BIS 'Extension of the Suspension of Expansion of End-User Controls for Affiliates of Certain Listed Entities', FR doc 2026-22793 (2026-11-09, to 2027-01-10). China, press-grade only: Reuters via internazionale.it and The Star (both 2026-11-09) report the Commerce Ministry extending its export-control pause 'for two months until January 10'; the MOFCOM/GAC text, announcement number and item list were not readable (english.mofcom.gov.cn reset the connection). Filed estimate: the Chinese leg rests on press, and the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a Federal Register notice or a MOFCOM announcement.
notes: PROPOSED AS THE SUCCESSOR TO THE EVENT THAT JUST CLOSED, NOT AS A NEW THEME. us-china-tariff-truce-expiry-2026-11-10's close-out (2026-11-12) scored both registered forward tests as papered over: each lapse (MOFCOM export-control suspension, USTR Sec. 301 maritime suspension, BIS Affiliates Rule suspension) was extended by two months rather than allowed to bite. The same three clocks now end together on 2027-01-10 (the USTR notice ends 11:59 p.m. ET on 2027-01-09), 59 days out and so inside the research horizon only now (it was 96 days out when earlier ledger rows named it and declined to propose it). The Trump-Xi meeting expected at APEC Shenzhen on 2026-11-18/19 is the next venue before it. Dates are estimates: nothing on the Chinese side has been read from MOFCOM's own text. Research only; an estimate widens caution and never licenses a position.
